impact: Performance only. What the user feels is the delay between clicking Settings and the dialog appearing; the renderer is not blocked meanwhile. fix: Minimal: take the GPU memory line off the critical path. At shell.js:2461-2466, start an un-awaited async block that awaits gpuMemoryMB() and cardMemory() and writes ui.setGpuMem.textContent, the same way refreshFileStats() at 2474 already runs. Optionally overlap the independent pairs: one keys.list result passed to both renderProviders and renderCompat; Promise.all of [loadProviders, prompts.list, helpers.status, plugins.list, info, updates.status], with each render still after its own data. Keep showModal at the end, or move it first only together with guards against the races below.
fix_risk: Small for the minimal fix: no gate reads #set-gpu-mem (grep over tools/ finds nothing). Showing the dialog first is riskier. showModal's initial focus would land before the rows exist (editor_test escape_closes_the_shell_dialogs reads activeElement). evidence: renderer/assistant.js:507-515: case text_delta calls streamText.appendData(e.text) and then if (atBottom()) ui.list.scrollTop = ui.list.scrollHeight, where atBottom (359-361) reads scrollHeight, scrollTop and clientHeight. Reading scrollHeight right after the text mutation forces a style and layout flush, once per text_delta IPC event. Main emits one event per streamed chunk with no batching (assistant/index.js:644; anthropic.js:215; gemini.js, chat.js and responses.js also call onText). The same pattern is in add() (363-367) and help.js:224-227, which sets scrollTop = scrollHeight unconditionally per delta. The proposed fix 'check atBottom before the append' does not remove the forced layout: the scrollTop = scrollHeight that follows still reads scrollHeight on a dirty layout, and the read before the append is itself forced whenever an earlier delta in the same frame dirtied the layout. Only coalescing the scroll per frame removes it. There is a functional point the review missed: checking after the append means one delta that adds more than 40 px stops the auto-follow although the user was at the bottom. The panel is 340 px wide at 13px/1.4 (assistant.css:15, 25), so about 18 px per line and roughly 45-50 characters per line; a chunk of about 130 characters or more adds three lines, and Gemini- or OpenAI-style chunks can be that long. Not covered by docs/BUGS.md or docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md; docs/PLAN_ASSISTANT.md (the List bullet near line 1879) only says the list 'stays at the bottom only while the user is already there'.
impact: Performance only, and small. The forced layout is local (the growing bubble's text is reshaped, then the flex column) and costs well under a ms per delta (inferred, not measured). The frame would lay out once anyway, so the forced flushes only cost extra when several deltas arrive within one frame (about 30-100 events per second while streaming). It shares the renderer's main thread with the editor, but the gain is a fraction of a ms per frame. No output bytes are involved.
fix: assistant.js:507-515 (and help.js:224-227 the same way): read stick = atBottom() before streamText.appendData. Then append, and if stick and no scroll is already scheduled, schedule one coalesced scroll (requestAnimationFrame(() => { scheduled = false; ui.list.scrollTop = ui.list.scrollHeight; })). While a scroll is pending, keep the stick decision instead of reading layout again.
fix_risk: The rAF trap: requestAnimationFrame does not fire in a hidden window (CLAUDE.md). Only the scroll may be deferred, never the appendData, or a gate or test that reads the streamed text before the end (PLAN_ASSISTANT.md test text_deltas_reach_the_panel_before_the_end; tools/assistant_test.js, assistant_mock.py) would see nothing in a hidden or occluded window. A deferred scroll that fires late is harmless. assistant:text (516-522) replaces the bubble and adjusts no scroll, so behaviour there stays as it is.
notes: The finding is right about the layout reads, but its fix is not the one that removes them. The more useful part is the auto-follow bug from checking after the append.

evidence: renderer/shell.js:3214-3220: reply = (r) => { let payload; try { payload = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify({ id, ...r })); } catch (err) { payload = { id, ok: false, error: 'the result is not JSON: ' + ... }; } window.scumble.commands.reply(payload); }, with the comment 'results are JSON by contract; anything else is an error, not a crash'. It has been there since the MCP phase (8b0de6d, 2026-09-09). preload.js:235 sends it with ipcRenderer.send('commands:reply'), which uses structured clone; bridge.js:28 resolves the pending call. The round trip is not redundant. (1) Structured clone throws on functions, DOM nodes, Promises and canvases. That throw would come out of the async onRequest handler as an unhandled rejection, and no reply would ever reach main: bridge.js:99 waits BASE_TIMEOUT (600 s) plus the command's timeout before 'did not answer in time'. The try/catch turns this into an immediate error reply. (2) Structured clone keeps Map, Set, typed arrays, Date, BigInt and cycles. The external MCP client receives JSON, but the in-app assistant gets the same result unserialised through InMemoryTransport (assistant/index.js:154-159). The round trip makes both see exactly the JSON shape: Map becomes {}, a typed array becomes an index object, and a cycle or BigInt is reported as an error instead of throwing later in main's JSON. The only large payload is screenshot's base64 JPEG (commands.js:2625-2643): max_size defaults to 1024 (about 0.1-0.4 MB) and goes up to 4096 (a few MB). export_layer and export_mask return a file path, not data. Not in docs/BUGS.md or docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md.
impact: Performance only, and negligible. JSON.stringify and JSON.parse of one long base64 string are fast paths: well under a ms at the default 1024 px, a few ms at the 4096 px maximum (inferred). Against that, the same command's canvas draw and toDataURL JPEG encode take tens to hundreds of ms, so the whole screenshot call would gain a few percent at most. There is no security angle.
fix: None needed. If ever wanted: send the string instead (payload = { id, json: JSON.stringify({ id, ...r }) }) and JSON.parse it in bridge.js _reply. That keeps the contract and the error path, saves the renderer's parse and the structured clone of the object tree, and costs one parse in main.
fix_risk: The string variant changes the commands:reply wire shape between preload, shell.js and bridge.js. Every sender of commands:reply has to change in step, including any test that fakes replies. Main would also do a parse it does not do today.
notes: Removing the round trip would bring back the 10-minute hang on a result that cannot be cloned, and would let the in-app assistant and external agents see differently shaped results.

evidence: Part 1 is in the code. electron/main/main.js:1069-1075 `probeComfy` takes `conn.url` and `conn.auth` from the caller and falls back to `keys.get(COMFY_SECRET)` whenever `conn.secret` is missing or empty, with no check that the url is the saved one. It is exposed as IPC `comfy:probe` (main.js:1095, preload.js:67) to the renderer's main world. Plugins are ES modules imported into that same world (renderer/plugins.js:829), so they can call it. Because `conn.auth` is also the caller's, `{url: <other host>, auth: {type: "header", header: "X-Anything"}}` sends the stored password or token as that header (comfy.js:20-29 `authHeaders` puts the secret under any header name). llm.js:116-124 `compatModels` does make the comparison the review describes (the key only when the base equals the saved base), and the providers' `baseUrl` allowlists (toapis.js:79-82, comfycloud.js:50-52) show the project treats a URL named by the renderer as a way to leak a key. The review misses three things. (a) `connectComfy` (main.js:984-995) does the same thing: a conn object without `secret`, or a plain URL string from the top bar, stores the new URL and sends `keys.get(COMFY_SECRET)` to it. (b) `settings:set` (preload.js:47, settings.js:114-118) takes any patch, including `comfy.url`, and the next `connectComfy()` (every start) sends the stored secret to that URL. So a URL check in `probeComfy` alone does not stop a malicious plugin. The same goes for llm.js's check, since `settings.llm.compat.url` is just as writable. (c) In the Settings dialog, Test and Connect with a URL the user changed (shell.js:352-360: the secret is sent only when typed) also send the stored secret to the new host, with no malice involved. Part 2 is also in the code. comfy.js:105 (`proxy`) and :134 (`probe`) fetch with `redirect: "follow"` and `this.headers`; `ComfyClient.fetch` (comfy.js:82-85, used by `connect`/`json`, uploads and so on) follows redirects by default as well. Node's undici fetch removes only authorization, proxy-authorization, cookie and host on a cross-origin redirect, so basic and bearer auth are dropped but an `auth.type === "header"` value goes on to the redirect target. Compare the ComfyUI window, which puts the same headers on the target's origin only (comfyview.js:125, 424-426).
impact: An external party cannot reach this. An opened file, an MCP agent and the ComfyUI server have no path to `comfy:probe`. No MCP command connects or probes (commands.js `set_settings` writes recipe rows only). The probe harvest needs a malicious plugin the user installed. Such a plugin already has other ways to the same secret (`settings.set` of `comfy.url` followed by connect, or `connect` directly), and it can read the secret field while the user types. The probe is one more path, not a new boundary crossing. The realistic case without malice is the user testing or connecting another server in the dialog and sending their own pod's token there. The redirect case needs the user's own ComfyUI or its reverse proxy to answer with a cross-origin 3xx; then the custom-header token for that server reaches the third host. That is rare (no such setup is documented), and a malicious server already has the header.
fix: Bind the stored secret to the origin it was stored for, not to whatever `settings.comfy.url` says at the time. In `connectComfy` (main.js:990), store the secret together with `originOf(saved.url)` (comfyview.js exports `originOf`), for example as JSON in the key store or as a second key. Add a helper `storedSecretFor(url)` that returns the secret only when `originOf(url)` equals the stored origin. Use it in `probeComfy` (main.js:1073), `connectComfy` (main.js:994) and `comfyTarget` (main.js:1001). This covers the dialog, plugin and `settings:set` cases together, which a plain comparison with the saved URL (the review's fix) does not. For redirects, use `redirect: "manual"` in `ComfyClient.fetch`, `proxy` and `probe` (comfy.js:84, 105, 134) and follow hops by hand (up to about 5), re-sending `this.headers` only while the hop's origin equals `this.url`'s origin. That is the pattern of the helper downloader fix in docs/BUGS.md:16-29 (`hfTokenAllowed`).
fix_risk: A user who changes the server's address (a new RunPod pod id or port) must type the secret again, because Test and Connect against the new origin send none and the server answers 401. The dialog should say so. Existing installs have a stored secret with no origin: migrate it by taking the saved `comfy.url`'s origin on first read. Following redirects by hand in `proxy` changes what the renderer sees for a 3xx (the status must stay the final hop's), and a reverse proxy that answers http to https with a redirect must still work: the same host with another scheme is a different origin, so the header is dropped there, which can break a setup that relies on it. Tests: the comfyview gate, the `platform` and `recipes` gates, and an `mcp` connect. The node build is not affected (main process only). No pixel bytes are involved.
notes: The review's claim that "llm.js compares base URLs" is correct but gives a false sense of safety: `settings:set` makes `settings.llm.compat.url` writable from the renderer, so a plugin bypasses that comparison as well. Severity should come down from medium to low: the only adversary who can call it is a user-installed plugin that already has full renderer IPC. The undici redirect behaviour comes from knowledge of undici's `httpRedirectFetch` and was not measured here.

evidence: electron/main/local.js:26-41 `lines()` does `buf += chunk` with no upper bound until a newline arrives, and runs `buf.indexOf("\n")` over the whole buffer on every chunk. local.js:62-69 `listen()` calls `this.server.listen(this.path)` with no chmod and no umask. On Linux the socket is `<userData>/scumble.sock` (local.js:20-24), so its mode follows the process umask. Started at main.js:118 and 1425. The header comment (local.js:4-5) says the design is "Local machine only, no authentication: the same trust as the DevTools port". The client side (`LocalClient`, local.js:112) uses the same unbounded `lines()`. Legitimately large lines exist: `select_mask` takes "an array of width*height values" as JSON (renderer/commands.js:1183-1184), and screenshots come back base64 (commands.js:2627-2641).
impact: The DoS needs a process that can write to the pipe or socket. On Windows a named pipe created with libuv's default security gives write access only to the creator owner, administrators and SYSTEM (Everyone gets read), so only the same user's code or an admin can send requests. Such code already holds the user's rights: it can drive every command through the same socket or simply end Scumble, so a memory DoS adds nothing. On Linux, connecting needs write permission on the socket file. With the usual umask (022, or 002 with per-user groups) other users cannot connect, so a chmod to 0o600 is defence in depth only. macOS does not ship (B3 not started), and the Linux socket path is marked "never exercised" (docs/BUGS.md:389). One side effect, inferred and not measured: because `indexOf` flattens and scans the whole growing string on every chunk, one very large line costs quadratic copying on the main process's thread (a 100 MB JSON line in 64 KB chunks is roughly 80 GB of copying, several seconds). That would hit a legitimate large `select_mask` sent over the socket, not only an attacker.
already_planned: docs/BUGS.md:389 lists the Linux unix socket as never exercised; neither point is covered.
fix: In local.js:26-41, keep the pending part as an array of chunks and search only the new chunk for "\n", so the cost stays linear. Add a cap of a few hundred MB, sized to the largest legitimate line such as a 15k `select_mask` array or a base64 image. Past the cap, answer `{id: null, ok: false, error: "line too long"}` and `socket.destroy()`. On non-Windows, call `process.umask(0o077)` around `this.server.listen(this.path)` in local.js:67 (restoring it in the listening callback), or `fs.chmodSync(this.path, 0o600)` in the `listening` event. The umask route avoids the window between bind and chmod.
fix_risk: A cap set too low breaks big MCP payloads through a running instance (`select_mask` arrays and data-URL masks for large pictures), and the `mcp` and `mcpb` gates would not catch it unless they send such a line. Changing `process.umask` is process-wide and briefly affects other files created at the same moment. The chmod only matters on Linux, which no gate exercises. No bytes or pixel paths change; the node build is not affected.
notes: The facts in the code are right, but medium overstates it: no other user or remote party can realistically reach the socket, and the same user can do anything anyway. The more useful part of a fix is the linear line splitter, which also helps large legitimate messages. Not checked: whether libuv sets PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS on the Windows pipe. Remote SMB access would in any case need write rights on the pipe, which the default DACL gives only to the owner and admins.

evidence: electron/main/recipes.js:852-857 `save(recipe)` writes `path.join(userDir(), recipe.id + ".json")` with no sanitising. There is no `userFile` function; the review's name is wrong, but the effect is as described. `remove` (recipes.js:845-850) strips everything except `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`. Every caller of `save` was traced: (1) `importFile` (recipes.js:1879-1883) sets `recipe.id = slug(...)`; its Comfy Cloud branch (1847-1859) goes through `fromCloudGraph` with `name: stem0`, which slugs (recipes.js:1440-1445). (2) `saveComfyGraph` (main.js:1027-1059) passes `fromGraph` or `fromCloudGraph`, which give either a slugged new id (recipes.js:1263-1268 and 1440-1445) or `base.id` (recipes.js:1261 and 1438). `base` is a listed recipe found by `heldId === r.id` (main.js:1029), and `heldId` is the id of the recipe the window opened (comfyview.js:509), not a value from the ComfyUI page. The bar's `comfyview:save` passes only `asNew` and `name` (comfyview.js:187). (3) `cloudCopy` (main.js:962-969) saves `recipes.detach(r)`, whose id is `` `${recipe.id}_cloud` `` (recipes.js:1801), for an `r` that must be a listed recipe. So an unsafe id reaches `save` only through a listed recipe's own id, and `readDir` (recipes.js:285-301) takes that from the JSON file's content unchecked (`r.id = r.id || n.replace(...)`). All 73 shipped recipes have ids matching `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` (checked in recipes/*.json).
impact: The only route is a recipe JSON with a crafted `"id": "..\\..\\x"` that the user copied by hand into `%APPDATA%/Scumble/recipes`. Import through the app slugs the id. The user must then press *Cloud copy*, or *Save to recipe* in the ComfyUI window on that recipe. Result: Scumble writes a recipe-shaped `.json` file at a path relative to the recipes folder within the user's own rights. An example is `"id": "../settings"` used with *Save to recipe*, which overwrites `%APPDATA%/Scumble/settings.json` with recipe JSON and resets the app's settings (keys are not affected). The `.json` suffix is fixed and the content is Scumble's own recipe shape, so code execution is not plausible. Nothing outside the user's hand-copied file can trigger it.
fix: In recipes.js:852-857, refuse an id outside `/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/`, and also check `path.dirname(file) === userDir()` before writing. Better still, sanitise once at the source: in `readDir` (recipes.js:292), drop or rename a recipe whose `r.id` fails that pattern, with a `console.warn` as for unreadable files. That way `base.id` and `` `${id}_cloud` `` can never carry a separator. Keeping `remove`'s pattern (recipes.js:846) makes the two agree.
fix_risk: Low. All 73 shipped ids already match. A user recipe saved earlier by the app has a slugged id. Only a hand-written user recipe with spaces or other characters in its `id` would vanish from the list, or be refused at `save`; warn rather than drop silently. Gates that create recipes: `recipes`, `comfyview`, `loras`. The node build is not affected (main process only).
notes: A side effect of the same gap: `remove(id)` deletes `<sanitised id>.json`, not the recipe's own file (`r.file`). A user recipe whose `id` differs from its file name therefore cannot be removed from *Settings › Recipes*, or the wrong file goes. A small correctness bug beside this one; using `r.file` in `remove` would fix both.

evidence: electron/main/main.js:434 really does `win.webContents.setWindowOpenHandler(({ url }) => { shell.openExternal(url); return { action: "deny" }; })` with no scheme check. The IPC path main.js:1312 (`app:openExternal`) and comfyview.js:285/314 check `/^https?:\/\//`. One small correction: those checks are case-sensitive (no /i). Only comfyhosts.js:38 `popupAction` uses /i. That is harmless, because an uppercase scheme is refused, not let through. No first-party code in the main window reaches this handler with an outside URL. renderer/ and plugins/ have no `window.open(` and no `_blank`. Every link is `<a href="#">` plus a click handler calling `window.scumble.openExternal` (shell.js:826, 2747, 2926, 2928; keydialog.js:498, 512). The manual reader (renderer/help/manual.js) and help.js use buttons, not anchors. assistant.js:15-16 and 55 builds model text with textContent ('a URL stays text'). The editor's innerHTML sites hold only icon markup (inpaint_canvas.js:1476 etc., host.js:2837). The CSP (index.html:5) has no 'unsafe-inline' for scripts. One reachable trigger exists: a middle-click (auxclick, which the click handlers do not catch) on one of the `href="#"` links. That most likely hands `scumble://app/index.html#` to openExternal, and Windows then shows its 'find an app for this link' prompt. Not run.
impact: Only code already running in the main window can use this to open a non-http URL: a user-installed plugin, or a future XSS (none found). Such code already has more power through the preload. `file:read` (main.js:1161, readFile at 850) reads any path, and `file:save` / `file:saveStart` take a renderer-given `path`. filesaves.js:45-61 checks size, folder, read-only and free space, but has no location rule, so renderer code can already write e.g. a .bat into the Startup folder. So the bypass of the http(s) rule (file:, smb: NTLM leak, ms-* handlers) adds no real power for an attacker who is already in the renderer. It is a defense-in-depth gap plus a small UX defect (the middle-click prompt). The review's high/medium is too high.
fix: main.js:434: `win.webContents.setWindowOpenHandler(({ url }) => { if (/^https?:\/\//i.test(String(url))) shell.openExternal(url); return { action: "deny" }; });`. Better still, one shared helper (e.g. `openHttp(url)`) used at main.js:434, main.js:1312, comfyview.js:285, 309 and 314.
fix_risk: None found. No first-party path opens a non-http window from the main window. tools/comfyview_test.py:244 tests window.open on the ComfyUI page, not the main window. No bytes and no node-build effect (main process only).
notes: Claim right, severity overstated: renderer code can already read and write any path through IPC. The real gain is consistency, plus no OS prompt on a middle-click of an href="#" link.

evidence: comfyview.js:304-310 (did-create-window): the child gets setMenu(null), setIgnoreMenuShortcuts and a setWindowOpenHandler, and no will-navigate or will-redirect guard. The page itself (wc, comfyview.js:311-315) has will-navigate but no will-redirect, so a server redirect is not checked there either. comfyhosts.js:17 `CLOUD_AUTH_HOSTS = ["cloud.comfy.org", ".comfy.org", ".firebaseapp.com", "accounts.google.com", "github.com"]` is confirmed. Correction: `github.com` matches exactly that host only (hostMatches, comfyhosts.js:19-21), not 'all of github.com' including subdomains, and github.com shows only sanitized user content. `.firebaseapp.com` is the broad entry: anyone can host arbitrary pages at <project>.firebaseapp.com. popupAction (comfyhosts.js:36-39) returns "child" on both targets. So the opener does not even need to navigate the popup: it can open `https://attacker.firebaseapp.com/` directly as a child. The host list matters more than the missing guard. The child is sandboxed, with contextIsolation, no nodeIntegration and no preload (comfyview.js:298). scumble:// is handled only on the default session (main.js:210 protocol.handle), not on persist:comfyui. Auth headers go only to the target's origin (requestPatterns, comfyview.js:115-120). Related, and not in the review: electron/main has no setPermissionRequestHandler or setPermissionCheckHandler for persist:comfyui (grep finds none). Electron's default approves every permission request (camera, mic, geolocation, notifications) for the page and its children.
impact: The attacker must already run JS in the ComfyUI page: a custom node pack's frontend on the user's server, or Comfy Cloud itself. On a local ComfyUI such a pack already runs Python on the user's PC, so there is nothing to gain. On a remote (RunPod) server the gain is a 520x720 'Sign in' window with no address bar showing attacker content: phishing for keys or passwords. It gets no IPC, no window.scumble, no scumble:// and no auth headers. The page's own view can already show the same content on its own origin, so the extra gain is small. The missing permission handler gives silent camera/mic access to the page whether or not this is fixed.
fix: (1) In comfyview.js did-create-window (304-310) add `child.webContents.on("will-navigate", (e, u) => { if (!cloudAuthUrl(u)) e.preventDefault(); })` and the same on `will-redirect` (export cloudAuthUrl from comfyhosts.js; it is already exported, line 50). (2) Narrow comfyhosts.js:17 `.firebaseapp.com` to the named project `dreamboothy.firebaseapp.com`. comfyhosts.js:5-6 says the Comfy account login uses it and Comfy Cloud uses 'the same Firebase'; confirm the cloud's authDomain in its bundle first. Add `https://evil.firebaseapp.com/` to the `no` list in tools/comfyhosts_test.js:15. (3) Worth more than both: `session.fromPartition(PARTITION).setPermissionRequestHandler((wc, perm, cb) => cb(perm === "clipboard-sanitized-write" || perm === "fullscreen"))`, plus a matching check handler.

evidence: Confirmed: (1) the inflate has no output cap. Window: renderer/editor/inpaint_canvas.js:577-580 `inflateBytes` = `new Response(stream).arrayBuffer()`. Its worker twin: inpaint_worker.js:511-514 `inflateZlib`. The PSD ZIP branch is inpaint_layered.js:122-126: `await inflate(r.bytes(dataLen))`, then keeps only `raw.subarray(0, Math.min(raw.length, out.length))`, so everything inflated past w*h*bpc is thrown away. ORA: readOra `get()` (:531-540) calls `inflateRaw(e.data)` with no cap. `unzip` (:500-520) reads csize (p+20) but never the uncompressed size (p+24). (2) Layer and mask rectangles are not bounded. inpaint_layered.js:363 reads top/left/bottom/right as i32. :389 `w = right-left, h = bottom-top`. :397 does the same for the mask rectangle (cw/chh from maskRecord's i32s, :202). The only guard before `readChannel`'s `new Uint8Array(w * h * bpc)` (:111) is `> 0` (:398, :401). layerMask allocates `new Uint8Array(w*h)` (:226). A RLE layer of 30000x30000 needs only its 2*h row-length table per channel (about 60 KB) in the file, yet allocates 0.9-1.8 GB per channel plus the RGBA bands. Wrong in the review: decodePsd itself checks no document size. The check is the caller's `checkLayeredSize` (inpaint_canvas.js:18595-18598: checkBaseSize 18392-18402, HUGE_MAX_SIDE 65535 / HUGE_MAX_PIXELS 2^30 on tiles, then 268 MP), not '1..30000'. On the pool route (D0) it runs on the header's 26 bytes before the job (readPsdOnPool 18612-18619). On the window fallback it runs only after the whole parse (18560-18562), and readPsd's merged picture (mergedPlanes, :315-335) is then sized from the unchecked header. Where the reader lives now: `readPsdStream` in the pool job `psd_read` (inpaint_worker.js:524-546, an error becomes `{failed}`). The window's `readPsd` stays as fallback and twin. ORA is read on the window only. Refuted as harmless: `const out = {}` (:507). An entry named "__proto__" only sets that object's own prototype, with no global pollution. A src of "constructor", "__proto__" or "method" resolves to an inherited value whose `.method` is undefined, so readOra throws 'unknown zip method' and the file is refused. The DataView reads in unzip are bounds-checked and throw a RangeError. `subarray` clamps, so a short entry fails in the inflater or the PNG decoder. JS stays memory-safe throughout.
impact: Who: anyone who gets the user to open a crafted .psd or .ora (from the web, a mail, a shared folder). What: denial of service only. A file of a few hundred KB asks the renderer (the worker runs in the same process) for several GB. A failed ArrayBuffer allocation throws a RangeError, so the open is refused; a successful one commits the memory and the machine swaps. A deflate bomb (about 1000:1, so 10 MB of channel data gives about 10 GB) builds up inside Blink's Response body reader, where an allocation failure most likely ends the whole renderer (not measured). Every open tab dies and work since the last autosave is lost. No code execution, no data read. Not medium for a single-user local app.

impact: Small. The HF token goes only to HF's own CDN on the redirect, and the template has never run. The unpinned clones are a supply-chain risk on the user's own rented pod, the same as any ComfyUI-Manager install at HEAD. No fork contributor ever holds a write token. The rest is that a compromised npm package or action tag running on a push to main gets a contents:write token for that run's lifetime (push commits or tags, edit draft releases). The tag runs need write in the same jobs anyway.
fix: build.yml: set `permissions: contents: read` at the top. Add `permissions: contents: write` to `draft` and `sizes` (both tag-only) and to `windows` and `linux` (their tag uploads need it), or move the uploads into a tag-only job that takes the artifacts. Add `with: persist-credentials: false` to the checkouts of the build jobs. provision.sh: use `curl -fL -H "Authorization: Bearer ..."` (curl drops a custom Authorization on a cross-host redirect unless --location-trusted) or `hf download`. Pin the clones to commits (`git -C dir checkout <sha>` after clone, no pull at start).
fix_risk: Splitting permissions wrongly breaks the tag build's uploads (electron-builder publish, gh release upload). That shows up only on the next release tag, so test it with a workflow_dispatch or a tag on a fork first. With persist-credentials false, any step that runs git push needs its own credentials (none does today). The provision.sh changes are untested in any case, since the template was never run.
notes: The review is right on the facts but not on the risk: on this public repo pull_request runs from forks never see the write scope. The global write only matters for supply-chain code that runs on the owner's own pushes.

evidence: True: crates/px/src/lib.rs multiplies unchecked in the older exports: mip_half :85-87, dist_transform :119/:122, flood :174/:181, grow_mask :192, flood_shape :213/:220, resample_block :243-246, composite_tile :265/:269, poisson :295. sel_combine (:431-444) checks size <= 4096 and uses `sel::source_bytes` with checked_mul (sel.rs:48-58). The release profile (crates/px/Cargo.toml) sets no overflow-checks, so the multiplications wrap; panic = "abort". Many kernels index through raw pointers or get_unchecked (resample.rs:92-138, edt.rs:85-113, composite.rs:644-866, mip.rs:119-161, sel.rs:242-268), so a short slice would be read or written past, not trapped. But no call reaches a kernel with a wrapped length. px.js does not bound w and h explicitly, but every input is copied in by `_in` (px.js:244-252: `new Uint8Array(data.buffer, off, bytes)` and `u8().set(src, ptr)`, both bounds-checked) and read out through `view` (:222-225). Rust's w*h*4 equals the JS number whenever that number is below 2^32, so a wrap needs w*h >= 2^30. Documents stop at HUGE_MAX_PIXELS = 2^30 on tiles (inpaint_canvas.js:654-655, checkBaseSize :18392-18402). The canvas route stops at 268 MP, and the per-tile kernels run at tile or block size. At exactly 2^30 px, bytes = 2^32: px_alloc receives ToInt32 = 0, returns null, px.js throws PxOutOfMemory (:193-205), and kernels.js `recovered` (:267-277) runs the JS twin. There is a latent defect, in px.js and not in Rust: for bytes > 2^32 (beyond any document) `px_alloc` gets bytes mod 2^32, a small block. PxArena.take (px.js:722-736) records the chunk at the JS size. `_in`'s copy then throws a RangeError that does not come from an export, so trapMark (:111-113) does not mark the instance and `recovered` rethrows. The false-sized first chunk survives `reset` (:739-750), and later jobs on that instance could write past the real block.
impact: None for security. Everything stays inside the wasm instance's linear memory (the sandbox), and the inputs are the app's own pixel buffers sized by the app, not by a file. The overflow is unreachable at any size Scumble opens. The latent px.js case would mean silent corruption inside one worker's instance (wrong pixels, or a later dlmalloc trap) only if some future caller asked for a single block above 4 GiB.
fix: px.js `alloc` (px.js:193-206): `if (bytes >= 2 ** 32) throw new PxOutOfMemory(bytes);` before calling px_alloc, so the ToInt32 wrap can never hand out a short block. That route goes to the twin, needs no wasm change and changes no bytes. Use `bytes > 0x7fffffff` to also respect Rust's isize::MAX slice precondition. Optional: the same checked_mul refusal as sel_combine in the Rust exports. That is a .rs edit, so px.wasm changes and build_px.py --check applies, and returning a refusal code from the void exports changes their signatures (an ABI bump).
fix_risk: The px.js guard affects only requests of 4 GiB or more (or 2 GiB or more with the stricter bound), which cannot succeed in wasm32 today anyway. px_test and the gates are unaffected. The Rust-side variant means a rebuild of both wasm builds and, if signatures change, a px_abi_version bump that px.js must accept.
notes: The JS side bounds w and h implicitly (document limits, tile sizes, bounds-checked copies, 4 GiB wasm32 memory), not by an explicit check before each export. K1's trap recovery covers traps and PxOutOfMemory but not a RangeError from the copy-in.

evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_compositor.js:1063-1064 sets viewport 0,0,W,H and disables BLEND. The module has no gl.enable, no scissor and no colorMask call, and the context belongs to the compositor alone (:326; no other module touches comp.gl). VS (:30-38) maps a_pos 0..1 through u_rect (-1,-1,2,2) onto the whole clip square, and COPY_FS (:251-256) writes texture(u_tex, v_uv) without blending. So the full-screen copy overwrites every pixel of dst, which makes three clears redundant: :1133-1134 (tile layer), :1160-1161 (canvas layer) and :1197-1198 (default framebuffer before the final copy). Two clears are needed: :1069-1070 (the empty backdrop) and :1098-1099 (the coverage target, where the base draws only its own rectangle). Location lookups are repeated: this.prog's at :1074-1082 once per frame, this.copy's at :1136-1140 and :1164-1168 per layer, and again at :1200-1202 at the end. Only atlasU is cached (:367-383).
impact: Not felt by the user. A GPU-stack pan frame is 0.1 ms median (docs/PERFORMANCE.md:1048). In W0's profiled pan_and_zoom row, getUniformLocation took 4.2 ms over about 160 frames, roughly 0.03 ms a frame (docs/measurements/w0_2026-10-23/native_15k.json, profile.natives). Each clear is a fast W x H GPU clear per layer. The real per-layer cost is the full-viewport copy itself, which the ping-pong design needs. Dropping the clears and caching the locations leaves the bytes identical.
fix: Delete the clears at inpaint_compositor.js:1133-1134, :1160-1161 and :1197-1198, and keep :1069-1070 and :1098-1099. Cache the u_rect, u_mode, u_opacity, u_size, u_hasClip and sampler locations of this.prog and this.copy, plus both a_pos locations, in the constructor beside atlasU (:367). Set copy's u_rect and u_tex once, since uniform values persist per program. Optionally replace the copy draw with blitFramebuffer(src.fb -> dst.fb, NEAREST), which is also exact. Only a dirty-rect copy (copying just what the previous layer changed) would save the copy's bandwidth, and that one has to respect the coverage pass.
fix_risk: No change to output bytes. Gates to run on tiles: composite (gpu vs 2d at 1:1), pixels, groups / clip. The node gets inpaint_compositor.js unpatched (docs/BUILD_NODE.md:164) and behaves the same. Cached locations stay valid until a relink, and after a context loss composite() returns null at :1027 anyway.
notes: Neither skins nor either backend rely on these clears. The compositor canvas is drawn with drawImage over a viewCanvas that was already cleared (inpaint_canvas.js:21766-21783). The canvas backend only changes which sources reach the compositor. GLCompositor only runs when no filter layer is shown (glCompositeUsable, inpaint_canvas.js:21654).

evidence: The cache miss is real. renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:933-934 builds noiseKey with org = info.origin, and :938 compares it. info.origin is [vp.x*vp.sx, vp.y*vp.sy] (inpaint_canvas.js:15562), and vp comes from viewportRegion (:21601-21618), whose x and y are floored per frame, so any pan of one image pixel misses. On a miss, :941-948 deletes the texture, calls grainNoiseCanvas(W,H) and texImage2D's that canvas. The filter runs again per pan anyway, because filterKey carries vp (:15477). The film look's grain stage takes the same path (plugins/film/filters.js:350, :390). The claim's 'on the CPU' is wrong. grainNoiseCanvas (inpaint_filters.js:192-206) is a Canvas 2D createPattern + fillRect of the cached 1024 tile into a viewport-size canvas, which is GPU-backed at that size. The CPU cell loop only builds the tile, cached per sigma, chroma and seed (:153-184).
impact: This exact design was measured at 2 ms per zoom step, down from 194 ms, on a 3326x1808 view (docs/PERFORMANCE.md:304-310). The whole 1:1 pan frame of perf_test's stack, which carries film.look with portra400 grain, is 2.5 ms (PERFORMANCE.md:1085) and 3.9 ms median in W0b (docs/measurements/w0b_2026-10-23/summary.txt:77). So the plausible gain is about 1 ms per pan frame on a grain or film-look stack that is already within budget; the noise's share was never measured on its own. The proposed fix does not keep the bytes in general. Both paths are meant to see the same field (inpaint_filters_gl.js:762-764: 'Both paths must see exactly the same field'), and the CPU path (inpaint_filters.js:242-246) and full-resolution passes read the canvas field. The pattern is drawn smoothed whenever s > 1 (:203). At 1:1 the default size 1.5 gives s = 1.5, and plates scale by plate_scale. GPU LINEAR / REPEAT sampling of the tile will not reproduce Skia's smoothed pattern bit for bit, so the 1:1 view would drift from the flatten (tools/composite_test.py's view-vs-full and FILTER_CHAIN steps) and from film_test's CPU/GPU twins.
fix: Byte-safe subset only. In SETUP.grain (inpaint_filters_gl.js:929-949), when there is no plate and s = Math.max(1, size) === 1 (smoothing off; at the default size that means zoomed out below about 0.67), export grainTileCanvas from inpaint_filters.js and bind it once per [sigma, chroma, seed] as a NEAREST texture. In mode 5 of the FS (:134), texelFetch it at ((x + round(ox)) mod 1024, (y + round(oy)) mod 1024), which is exactly the pattern's integer shift. Keep today's W x H canvas for s > 1 and for plates. No change to the CPU twin.
fix_risk: Adds a shader branch and a uniform in FS mode 5, plus texture-unit-3 bookkeeping (the cached noise texture is deleted on a key change at :941). Tests and callers to watch: film_test's CPU/GPU twins and its None-grain check, composite_test FILTER_CHAIN, and the film plugin's own cache (`{...info, cache}`, plugins/film/filters.js:390). inpaint_filters_gl.js ships into the node build.
notes: docs/BUGS.md names no grain pan cost. docs/PERFORMANCE.md §2 describes the design and its cost. The bigger per-frame costs of a filter pan are the region pass and the filter's upload and readback, not the noise.

evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:782-792 runs whenever info.cache is set and src is a canvas: makeCanvas of at most 256 px, a drawImage of the whole input, a getImageData, and a luma histogram into info.cache.histogram. Nothing checks whether the input changed or the panel is open. filteredCanvas's early cache hit (inpaint_canvas.js:15545) skips it only when the key and compositeVersion match. A curves tick (layer.params in filterKey, :15470) re-runs it on an unchanged input, and so does every pan (vp in the key, :15477). It is also dead work on screen. Every screen pass is a view pass (drawSceneImage -> drawViewComposite, :23843 and :21788), whose cache slot is layer._fxCacheView (:15558). The curve editor reads only layer._fxCache.histogram (inpaint_filters.js:862), the full-resolution slot. So the histogram computed on screen is never read.
impact: Each curves run in a view pass costs one extra canvas, a downscaling draw of the viewport-size composite and a getImageData, which syncs with everything already queued on the GPU. Not measured (no perf row has a curves layer); plausibly 0.5-2 ms per pan frame or per curves tick, inferred. Removing it changes no output bytes.
already_planned: docs/PLAN_NIK9_BUILD.md:178 ('The curves histogram is probably missing on the tile backend's view passes (it reads _fxCache, view passes write _fxCacheView)') and :1051 ('Curves can later take its histogram from the same place', i.e. belowHistogram). Both cover the missing histogram in the panel; neither names the wasted readback.
fix: Point curvesControl (inpaint_filters.js:862) at the editor's belowHistogram(layer).luma (inpaint_canvas.js:15689). The range bars already use it (:19960), and it is cached per composite version. Then drop the histogram block from SETUP.curves (inpaint_filters_gl.js:780-792); the CPU applyCurves histogram (inpaint_filters.js:850-853) can go too. Minimal alternative: compute it only when the pass writes the _fxCache slot, via an info flag that filteredCanvas sets when vp is null.
fix_risk: The panel would start showing a histogram on screen, where today it usually shows none or a stale one. No pixel output changes. curvesControl needs a way to reach the editor (it already gets callbacks). No test reads .histogram (grep over tools/). The node ships the same editor files.
notes: The fault is on both backends, not only tiles: the slot depends on viewPass alone (inpaint_canvas.js:15558).

evidence: True that no GL path exists: SUPPORTED (renderer/editor/inpaint_filters_gl.js:143) and SETUP (:771-954) have no fill or gradient, so applyFilterGL returns null (:1186). applyFilter then calls f.apply with the input as it is, because f.chain is set (inpaint_filters.js:1352-1355). But `chain: true` (:1279-1281, :1288, :1307) means 'apply() takes a GPU surface and reads only its size', so the fill itself reads nothing back. The chain flush at a fill layer is by design and would happen with or without a SETUP entry: isFillLayer makes `plain` false (inpaint_canvas.js:16184), so keepSurface is false and flushFilterChain runs (:16193). A SETUP.fill would not keep the chain. The real per-pan cost: fillApply's key holds full and origin (inpaint_filters.js:571-574). A gradient therefore re-runs fillPixels over the whole viewport in JS (:520-565) plus putImageData (:578) every pan frame. A colour fill makes a new canvas plus fillRect (:577) every pan frame, although its bytes depend only on W and H. With any filter layer shown, the screen runs on Canvas 2D (inpaint_canvas.js:21654).
impact: Affects gradient fill layers only. Not measured: no perf row has a fill layer, but `perf_test.py --filter=gradient` would measure it. Inferred at a few ns per pixel, that is about 10-20 ms per pan frame on a 2560x1440 view plus the upload. The colour fill costs a canvas allocation per frame. A GLSL gradient would not keep bytes: fillPixels rounds f64 into a 1,024-entry table (:529-561), and float32 maths moves the index at rounding edges. That breaks PLAN_0_1_31.md:880-883's rule that 'every pass gives the same bytes'.
fix: Colour fill: key [id, p.color, W, H] in fillApply (inpaint_filters.js:572) so a pan reuses its canvas; the bytes stay the same. Gradient: measure first. If it matters, use a twin that keeps the f64 maths (a pool job, or a px kernel that keeps JS Math.round semantics) instead of a GLSL SETUP. Do not add SETUP.fill.
fix_risk: The fill gate (tools/fill_test.py: colour fill byte for byte on flatten and export, gradient within 1 level of floats), the clipDoc path (inpaint_canvas.js:16254-16259), and the cached canvas reused across W/H changes (keep W and H in the key). The exports' fillLayerRows call fillPixels directly and are unaffected.
notes: The design is PLAN_0_1_31.md §6 step 6 (:876-900). fillPixels runs only for gradients; the colour fill never calls it.

evidence: renderer/editor/inpaint_tiles.js:1139-1164, put(): per pixel it reads the alpha byte, then writes four bytes (opaque), four zeros (transparent) or four premultiply-table bytes. S = 258 at level 0 (:1124), so up to 66,564 px per slot. coarseSlot (:1192-1205) tests the opaque and transparent 32-bit words first (LITTLE / ALPHA :82-83, words() :529-531, u32Of :471). It runs on the main thread from the compositor's _upload (inpaint_compositor.js:860). In W0's profiled pan_and_zoom row, put's self time is 332 ms against 5 ms for tileWithGutter and 30 ms for 540 texSubImage2D calls (137 MB) (docs/measurements/w0_2026-10-23/native_15k.json). Unprofiled, W0b's row is 340 ms and the 1:1 far-pan frame 12.2 ms median, 16.4 ms max (docs/measurements/w0b_2026-10-23/summary.txt:42). docs/PLAN_BCE.md:2014 puts the 15-17 ms left at 1:1 after a whole change on 'the 40 level-0 slots' premultiply and upload', about 6 ns/px.
impact: Affects every frame that uploads new level-0 slots: a far pan at 1:1, a zoom to 1:1, and the landing frames after a whole change at 1:1. Opaque photo tiles and empty paint tiles take the word path. Plausibly 3-5x off put (inferred), which would bring the 1:1 far-pan frame from about 12 ms toward 5-7 ms, to be measured. Bytes stay identical: a word with alpha 255 copied whole and a zero-alpha word written as 0 are exactly what the byte path writes, and every other pixel keeps the table path.
fix: In tileWithGutter (inpaint_tiles.js:1139-1164), make o32 = LITTLE ? words(out) : null once per call. Make one word view per neighbour info, also once: u32Of(t) for level-0 tile data, words(info.data) for chains, edge copies and primed cells, cached beside near[]. Use u32Of(info.t) in the coarse branch. In both loops, test the word first exactly as coarseSlot does at :1200-1205 (>= 0xFF000000: copy the word; < ALPHA: write 0), then fall through to the existing byte path. No Rust is needed.
fix_risk: The pixels gate's atlas cases and their mutation round (gutter, clamp extension, premultiply: PLAN_BCE.md:1228, :1296) must stay as they are. Fallbacks: words() returns null for a misaligned view and on big-endian, which keeps the byte path. A typed-array view made per row or per put() call instead of per info would eat the gain. inpaint_tiles.js ships into the node build.
notes: Measure as PLAN_WASM_BUILD §1.1 asks, on whole-operation wall time: w0_bench / perf_test pan_and_zoom and 'pan at 1:1 far' on three fresh instances, before and after. This is the only one of P6-P10 with a measured, user-felt cost. No K session in docs/PLAN_WASM_BUILD.md covers the atlas slot premultiply.
